content:
Marta: FYI seeing duplicate fragments when we preempt an active streaming conn during a model swap. Sometimes clients get repeated chunks, sometimes the stream cuts mid-token.
AJ: Is this during graceful preempt or kill path?
Marta: Graceful. We try to hand off to fallback model but the edge sometimes replays fragments.
Sam: Could the client be reconnecting and reissuing the request?
Marta: I checked the deploy logs and @deploy-bot shows a single upstream call. The replay seems internal to the proxy windowing logic.
Neel: Can you paste a sample from the ingress log?
Marta: Snippet below: 
```
--FRAME--
seq=1024
payload="...bring the"
--FRAME-END--
--FRAME--
seq=1024
payload="...bring the"
--FRAME-END--
```
Marta: exact same seq duplicated.
AJ: Same connection id? If so likely we re-enqueued instead of advancing the resume token.
Sam: My hunch: race between checkpoint commit and preempt. If checkpoint isn't persisted, replay will resend identical seq.
Neel: We have options: 1) preempt blocks until a soft checkpoint is flushed (adds tail latency), or 2) emit idempotency markers per fragment and dedupe downstream (needs cache or client support).
AJ: Dedupe cache at proxy could blow up for very long sessions unless we bound it. Client-side idempotency is nicer but requires API change.
Marta: Another idea: issue a tombstone resume token on preempt which claims the last confirmed seq. Then any fragments <= tombstone-seq get dropped by resume. Low latency, but stronger contract.
Sam: Tombstone works for read-only streams. For in-stream side effects (tool calls) dropping duplicates might hide retries and break exactly-once semantics.
Neel: Exactly. For tool-calls we either accept replay (and require app-level idempotency), or we route side-effectful fragments to an authoritative executor to ensure single execution. Both are heavier.
AJ: Pragmatic path: enable tombstone resume by default but mark routes with side-effects as `resume.supports_side_effects=false` and fall back to draining preempt for those.
Marta: Proposed route config example: 
```
ingress:
  preempt: graceful
  resume:
    enabled: true
    tombstone_lease: 128
    supports_side_effects: false
```
Sam: We also need observability: metrics like `edge.resume.tombstone_issued`, `edge.resume.duplicates_dropped`, and `edge.resume.replay_attempts`.
AJ: Trailers: if upstream emits an `X-Resume-Token` trailer, bind it atomically to the last-acked seq. Race happens when preempt triggers before trailer binding finishes.
Marta: Agreed. Agent should only publish token after we finish the frag ack loop so the resume token reflects committed state. That increases tail-latency slightly but reduces mismatches.
Neel: Long-term we should push idempotency keys at the application protocol (e.g., UUID per logical user response). That would allow safe dedupe without tombstones. It's a bigger API change though.
Sam: For short-term: I'll draft a small RFC + impl plan for tombstone resume + route flag for side-effects, plus tests and metrics.
Marta: I'll add a fuzz/regression test that injects preempt mid-stream and asserts no duplicate side-effect invocations for routes flagged as non-resumable.
AJ: Quick debug query if anyone needs traces: https://grafana.company/d/streams?query=duplicates_dropped&conn=ingress-1024
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: ingress/edge-v3 rollout at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (no code changes yet). :robot_face:
Marta: Thanks all, will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
